title: Small-bias Fourier estimation error
statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let a sample of $m$ points in the binary cube induce a probability density whose nonconstant Fourier coefficients have absolute value at most $\delta$, where $\delta\ge0$. Then the absolute difference between the sample estimate of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$ and its uniform Fourier coefficient is at most $\delta$ times the sum of the absolute values of all Fourier coefficients of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
$U$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
The sample is a map from an $m$-element index set to the binary cube of dimension $n$
The sample's uniform pushforward density has every nonzero binary Fourier coefficient bounded in absolute value by $\delta$
